site.name: codekite
site.summary: codekite-clone Fictional cloud CI/CD service "CodeKite CI" marketing site, focused on the pricing-page usage calculator. Pages | File | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `index.html` | Short landing: hero (YAML code example on the right), 3 feature cards, CTA to pricing | | `pricing.html` | Main page: 3 plan cards (Free / Team / Enterprise) + usage calculator (three slider+number pairs linked two-way: build minutes / concurrency / storage + ARM / macOS / GPU runner checkboxes); right-side sticky monthly total + recommended-plan badge + line-item cost breakdown; below: 16-row plan comparison table; 10-question FAQ accordion; trusted-logo row; 4-column footer | | `docs.html` | Placeholder quickstart page (one YAML example) |

run_plan.goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the full codekite system, prioritizing the primary pricing flow plus adjacent pages, states, and recovery paths.
run_plan.summary: The exploration will start by traversing the landing page and adjacent navigation to establish context, then dive deeply into the pricing calculator's interactive states and edge cases. It will validate the comparison table and FAQ accordion, check the docs page, and finally repeat critical interactive checks on a mobile viewport to assess responsiveness and tap target issues.
assumptions: The pricing calculator sliders and number inputs are two-way bound and should update the sticky monthly total and line-item breakdown dynamically.
The FAQ section contains an accordion that expands and collapses on click.
Footer links and the 'Sign in' link point to '#' or are non-functional placeholders.
The recommended-plan badge on the pricing page updates based on the slider/input values.
risk_hotspots: pricing.html: Two-way binding between sliders and number inputs (risk of desync or state bugs)
pricing.html: Sticky monthly total and line-item cost breakdown accuracy when toggling ARM/macOS/GPU checkboxes
pricing.html: Missing input labels on calculator controls (flagged in prescan)
index.html: Small tap targets for navigation links (flagged in prescan)

phases.title: Landing & Navigation Flow
phases.objective: Validate the main entry point, value proposition, and primary navigation paths to the pricing and docs pages.
key_checks: Verify hero section content and YAML code example visibility
Click 'See pricing' CTA and confirm navigation to pricing.html
Click 'Read docs' CTA and confirm navigation to docs.html
Click 'Start free trial' header button and confirm navigation to pricing.html
Check footer link behavior (expect no-op or placeholder)
exit_criteria: All primary CTAs on index.html have been clicked and verified
Navigation to all other known pages has been successfully executed

phases.title: Pricing Calculator Core Interactions
phases.objective: Exhaustively test the usage calculator to ensure inputs, two-way binding, and dynamic cost calculations function correctly.
key_checks: Drag 'Build minutes' slider and verify corresponding number input updates, and vice versa
Drag 'Concurrent builds' slider and verify corresponding number input updates, and vice versa
Drag 'Storage' slider and verify corresponding number input updates, and vice versa
Type extreme/out-of-bound values into number inputs and verify slider/error handling
Toggle 'Linux ARM runners' checkbox and verify line-item cost and total update
Toggle 'macOS runners' checkbox and verify line-item cost and total update
Toggle 'GPU runners' checkbox and verify line-item cost and total update
Verify recommended-plan badge updates appropriately when crossing plan thresholds
exit_criteria: All 3 slider/input pairs have been manipulated in both directions
All 3 runner checkboxes have been toggled on and off
Sticky total and breakdown have been verified to reflect input changes

phases.title: Pricing Page Content & Adjacent Elements
phases.objective: Validate the static content, comparison table, and interactive FAQ section on the pricing page.
key_checks: Scroll through and verify visibility of the 16-row plan comparison table
Click at least 3 different FAQ accordion items to ensure they expand/collapse correctly
Verify 'Get started', 'Start trial', and 'Talk to sales' buttons are present and clickable
Check for layout shifts or overlapping elements around the sticky total on scroll
exit_criteria: Comparison table has been scrolled into view
FAQ accordion interactions have been successfully validated
Plan CTA buttons have been identified and clicked

phases.title: Docs & Secondary Pages
phases.objective: Verify the documentation quickstart page content and ensure consistent navigation back to the pricing flow.
key_checks: Verify Quickstart YAML example is visible and formatted correctly
Click 'Pricing' in the header nav and confirm return to pricing.html
Click 'CodeKite' logo and confirm return to index.html
exit_criteria: Docs page content has been verified
Navigation back to index.html and pricing.html works correctly

phases.title: Mobile Viewport Validation
phases.objective: Re-test critical flows and layout stability on a mobile viewport, specifically addressing prescan tap target warnings.
key_checks: Verify index.html layout adapts to mobile width and hero content is readable
Check if navigation collapses into a hamburger menu or remains inline (assess tap target severity)
Interact with the pricing calculator sliders/inputs on mobile to ensure they are usable and not blocked by the sticky total
Verify the 16-row comparison table is scrollable or responsive on small screens
Validate FAQ accordion tap targets on mobile
exit_criteria: Mobile layout has been checked on index.html
Pricing calculator has been interacted with on mobile
Tap target and responsive layout issues have been documented

coverage_targets.features: exercise all calculator inputs/checkboxes, FAQ accordion, and primary CTAs
coverage_targets.mobile: repeat critical checks on mobile viewport, focusing on pricing calculator and tap targets

notes: Prescan flagged missing input labels on the pricing calculator; verify if visual labels exist but are improperly associated, or if they are completely missing.
Pay close attention to the sticky total behavior on mobile, as it may overlap with calculator controls.

prescan_summary.title: CodeKite CI — Faster builds. Honest bills.
prescan_summary.visible_text_excerpt: CodeKite Product Pricing Docs Sign in Start free trial Faster builds. Honest bills. CodeKite is a CI/CD service that bills you for what you build. No per-seat tax. Bring your .yml and a credit card you'll hopefully never max out. See pricing Read docs version: 2.1 jobs: build: runs-on: linux/x86 steps: - checkout - run: pnpm install - run: pnpm test - cache: path: node_modules key: lock-{{ checksum "pnpm-lock.yaml" }} Parallelism, plain Split a 12-min suite across 16 slots; pay per minute, not per slot. Slots scale to zero when idle. Bill you can read Every invoice breaks down to the job, the runner type, and the minute. Per-team and per-pipeline rollups. Drop-in YAML If you've used Circle or GitHub Actions, you're 90% of the way there. We provide a converter. CodeKite CI Faster builds. Honest bills. PRODUCT Overview Pricing Docs RESOURCES Changelog Status Security COMPANY About Blog Car

prescan_summary.title: CodeKite Docs
prescan_summary.visible_text_excerpt: CodeKite Product Pricing Docs Sign in Quickstart Drop a .codekite.yml at the root of your repo and push. version: 2.1 jobs: test: runs-on: linux/x86 steps: - checkout - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile - run: pnpm test --shard $CK_SHARD/$CK_TOTAL_SHARDS parallel: 8 That's it. Push a commit — your first build runs in under a minute. Local demo for UXBench. Fictional product, not a real company.

We'll suggest a plan and break the bill down line-by-line. What happens if I exceed Free-tier minutes? Are there hard caps on Team/Enterprise? Do you offer committed-use discounts? Where do builds run? Can I run my own runners? How is "concurrent builds" measured? Do you integrate with HashiCorp Vault? What counts as a "user" on Team? Refunds? observation.title: CodeKite CI — Faster builds. Honest bills.
observation.visible_text: CodeKite Product Pricing Docs Sign in Start free trial Faster builds. Honest bills. CodeKite is a CI/CD service that bills you for what you build. No per-seat tax. Bring your .yml and a credit card you'll hopefully never max out. See pricing Read docs version: 2.1 jobs: build: runs-on: linux/x86 steps: - checkout - run: pnpm install - run: pnpm test - cache: path: node_modules key: lock-{{ checksum "pnpm-lock.yaml" }} Parallelism, plain Split a 12-min suite across 16 slots; pay per minute, not per slot. Slots scale to zero when idle. Bill you can read Every invoice breaks down to the job, the runner type, and the minute. Per-team and per-pipeline rollups. Drop-in YAML If you've used Circle or GitHub Actions, you're 90% of the way there. We provide a converter. CodeKite CI Faster builds. Honest bills. PRODUCT Overview Pricing Docs RESOURCES Changelog Status Security COMPANY About Blog Careers Local demo for UXBench. Fictional product, not a real company.

observation.title: CodeKite CI — Faster builds. Honest bills.
observation.visible_text: CodeKite Product Start free trial Faster builds. Honest bills. CodeKite is a CI/CD service that bills you for what you build. No per-seat tax. Bring your .yml and a credit card you'll hopefully never max out. See pricing Read docs version: 2.1 jobs: build: runs-on: linux/x86 steps: - checkout - run: pnpm install - run: pnpm test - cache: path: node_modules key: lock-{{ checksum "pnpm-lock.yaml" }} Parallelism, plain Split a 12-min suite across 16 slots; pay per minute, not per slot. Slots scale to zero when idle. Bill you can read Every invoice breaks down to the job, the runner type, and the minute. Per-team and per-pipeline rollups. Drop-in YAML If you've used Circle or GitHub Actions, you're 90% of the way there. We provide a converter. CodeKite CI Faster builds. Honest bills.
